messages.author: 93f4be15fbe026a4
messages.subject: procD.lm output
parts:
Hi all,

I was wondering if anyone had any input about why the p-values shown in the output from my procD.lm do not change even when I change/ add in new terms to the model? The other values (MS, Rsq, Z etc.) change however, all of the p-values always remain the exact same. Just curious as to why this may be as it seems really odd.

Thanks!
Chelsea

messages.author: aab55242ff4da6c6
messages.subject: Re: [geomorph-r-package] procD.lm output
parts:
Chelsea,

This is a guess without additional information about SS.type, but if you are adding terms sequentially, Z-scores based on F-values can change (because the Residual SS changes) but the rank order of the values in the random permutations might stay the same, so the P-values do not change.  I would not expect SS, MS, or Rsq to change with SS.type = “I” and no order of terms changed, unless you are targeting on Residuals, which will naturally change because of additional terms.

Note also that P-values depend on the number of permutations and the seed used.  Without making changes to these, the value will stay the same with re-analysis (because the set of random permutations is the same).

What would be really odd is if when adding more terms, sequentially, P-values changed for the first terms in the model.  If you use conditional (type = II) or marginal (type = III) SS, the expectation of P-value constancy when adding more terms would be odd, as in these cases effects are conditioned on other effects.

Hope that helps! -Mike

messages.author: aab55242ff4da6c6
messages.subject: Re: [geomorph-r-package] procD.lm output
parts:
OK, with that in mind, if you add more terms to a model, you change the SS. MS, and Rsq for terms that were already in the model because the SS is calculated with respect to other terms in the model, which has changed.  So let’s say this has the effect of reducing SS for term A.  If it decreases SS for term A in a similar way in every random permutation, the rank of the observed SS in the distribution of random SS might not change at all, so the P-value stays the same.

A Z-score is based on the dispersion of the sampling distribution of the statistic used (F by default).  P-values only consider the rank of values.  So P-values might be less sensitive to changes.

I do wish to emphasize strongly to all reading this that I am not saying P-values should be the same, no matter what.  There is a logical reason that they could stay the same; there is also possible ways for them to change.   It depends on many things, like the size of effect, interaction of effects, etc.

Cheers!
Mike
